newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS TEES OFF ON HISTORIC MASTERS MARCH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS TEES OFF ON HISTORIC MASTERS MARCH.

text.p: Tiger Woods slashed his first-hole tee shot dead centre down the fairway as he set off on what could be an historic final round at the Masters Tournament on Sunday.

The 21-year-old Woods led by a record nine strokes after Saturday's third round, poised to become the youngest champion in Masters history and the first non-white player to ever win a major championship.
It was a breezy day at Augusta National, a condition that sometimes produces bizarre scoring at the Masters.
Ben Crenshaw, who won his second Masters title in 1995, posted a six-over-par 11 on the par-5 15th hole among the early starters on Sunday.

A few of the players far behind Woods on the leaderboard improved on their scores in the early going. Two-time champion Tom Watson birdied the first and second holes to move to six under par, nine shots behind the runaway leader.
Tom Kite, the 1992 U.S. Open champion, birdied the par-5 second hole to move to five under par.

Woods, who needs a round of 69 to break the Masters scoring record held jointly by Jack Nicklaus and Raymond Floyd, began the day at 15-under-par 201 after shooting 65 on Saturday to pad his lead from three strokes to nine.

He was playing the final round with Costantino Rocca of Italy. Rocca, who lost in a playoff for the 1995 British Open, was paired with Woods after finishing the third round at six-under 210 after shooting 69.
